_source: Hand-curated from internal/gateway/connector setup paths and hook profiles plus cli/defenseclaw/inventory/hook_contracts.json. Re-extract on every connector or hook-contract change.
_order: By adoption / popularity — mirrors the hero rotation (lib/hero-connectors.ts) and the docs nav (content/docs/connectors/meta.json).

connectors.label: Claude Code
connectors.summary: Native lifecycle hooks, native approval, and OpenTelemetry export.
connectors.hilt: Claude Code supports native PreToolUse ask prompts. CRITICAL findings still block; HIGH findings can pause for approval.
connectors.notes: Hook-only connector — no proxy data path and no DefenseClaw subprocess sandbox or command shims. The shared floor is >=2.1.154; macOS also requires <2.1.219, while Windows keeps the open ceiling. Native logs and metrics are configured on supported hosts, but enhanced beta traces are macOS-only and Windows traces remain disabled. Both native platforms remain preview/uncertified.

connectors.label: Codex
connectors.summary: Config hooks, native OpenTelemetry, and an agent-turn completion bridge.
connectors.hilt: Codex has no native ask surface here; confirm becomes an alert/systemMessage with raw_action preserved. The TUI can review the event but cannot resume it.
connectors.notes: Three telemetry channels at boot: hooks, native OTel, and the notify bridge for agent-turn-complete events. Hook-only connector — no proxy data path and no DefenseClaw subprocess sandbox or command shims.

connectors.label: OpenClaw
connectors.summary: Reference proxy with bundled fetch interception and before-tool-call enforcement.
connectors.hilt: OpenClaw supports DefenseClaw approval prompts for tool actions. Approvals reach chat-origin sessions via the bundled plugin.
connectors.notes: Reference proxy connector — full data-path interception, sandbox enforcement, plugin-mediated HITL.

connectors.label: Cursor
connectors.summary: Pre-execution shell and MCP hooks with native ask support.
connectors.hilt: Cursor enforces native ask only on beforeShellExecution and beforeMCPExecution. preToolUse accepts ask in the schema but does not enforce it; subagentStart confirm is downgraded to deny because that event accepts allow/deny only.
connectors.notes: hooks.json under ~/.cursor; command hooks fail open by default and use failClosed=true only for an explicit closed failure mode. sessionStart/sessionEnd are fire-and-forget and Stop is followup-only. Native macOS and Windows are preview pending durable packaged and authenticated official-client certification. DefenseClaw discovers documented Cursor local plugins, skills, and custom subagents without modifying discovery-only surfaces; editor extensions, nested AGENTS.md traversal, custom commands, and separate microagents are not managed.

connectors.label: Hermes
connectors.summary: Preview native lifecycle hooks with valid-JSON pre-tool blocking and unconditional failure-open behavior.
connectors.hilt: Hermes has no native human-approval surface; confirm verdicts are recorded and alerted but cannot pause or resume the hook.
connectors.notes: Preview/not certified on native macOS and Windows. Hooks live in $HERMES_HOME/config.yaml (default ~/.hermes on macOS and %LOCALAPPDATA%/hermes on Windows). hermes-hooks-v1 accepts >=0.19.0,<0.20.0 on macOS/Linux; Windows preserves >=0.19.0 with no ceiling. macOS registers the absolute executable POSIX hook asset; Windows registers a directly quoted absolute native defenseclaw-hook.exe argv. Hermes parses both with shlex.split and runs shell=False. All 23 Hermes v0.19 VALID_HOOKS events are registered and classified independently. Only valid synchronous pre_tool_call block JSON vetoes a tool; pre_llm_call may inject context and pre_verify may continue a bounded verification loop. Transform, API, gateway, approval, Kanban, and ordinary lifecycle events are audit-only in DefenseClaw's shell lane unless the official shell parser proves an effect. Timeout, nonzero exit, malformed output, authentication, and transport failures warn and continue; exit status is not enforcement. Hermes's separate upstream terminal tool uses installer-managed PortableGit/Git Bash on Windows and is outside DefenseClaw integration. Discovery covers canonical mcp_servers, local and configured external skills, read-only user/project plugins, shell and gateway hook packages, and context/rule files. Hermes 0.19.1 native monitoring.export.otlp is upstream-owned gateway-health telemetry; DefenseClaw policy telemetry remains hook-derived.

connectors.label: OpenCode
connectors.summary: Auto-loaded bridge plugin with tool-execution blocking.
connectors.hilt: No native human-approval surface; blocks by throwing in the bridge plugin's tool.execute.before. confirm verdicts fall back to allow.
connectors.notes: OpenCode contracts differ by platform. macOS/Linux accepts >=1.16.2,<1.18.11 and uses the 35-event v7 bridge; Windows preserves its unbounded/default range and nine-event v6 bridge and remains preview pending packaged Setup plus official-client evidence. The DefenseClaw JS plugin auto-loads from OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR/plugins/defenseclaw.js or ~/.config/opencode/plugins/defenseclaw.js without editing opencode.json. tool.execute.before throws to block; tool.execute.after and generic events are observe-only. Fail-closed applies only to the awaited before hook. Upstream 1.18.10 has experimental OTLP logs/traces, but DefenseClaw does not configure or certify them and the registry remains native_otlp=false.

connectors.label: OmniGent
connectors.summary: Custom policy bridge with allow, ask, and deny enforcement.
connectors.hilt: OmniGent parks request, tool_call, and llm_request for native ASK approval. Post-phase confirm findings are audited and continue without a pause; DENY may suppress onward-visible content but cannot roll back completed work.
connectors.notes: The documented custom Python policy bridge maps all six OmniGent policy phases. Post-phase DENY uses OmniGent's denial/sentinel behavior rather than custom replacement data. Optional native OTLP is inactive until the launch process sets OMNIGENT_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=true and exports the standard OTEL environment variables; OmniGent 0.7.0 includes logs, metrics, and traces in its base/default dependency set.

connectors.label: Gemini CLI
connectors.summary: Settings hooks with a native OTLP exporter pointed at the gateway.
connectors.hilt: Can block supported hook events but has no native human-approval surface; confirm verdicts fall back explicitly.
connectors.notes: settings.json hooks; native OTLP exporter wires directly to the gateway.

connectors.label: GitHub Copilot CLI
connectors.summary: Global or workspace hooks with native approval on pre-tool-use.
connectors.hilt: Copilot CLI supports native ask on documented preToolUse hooks.
connectors.notes: Windows/macOS/Linux 1.0.76+ selects the 14-event v2 contract, including audit-only userPromptTransformed; 1.0.18 through 1.0.75 selects the 13-event v1 contract. Native Windows remains not certified. Upstream can emit native OTLP traces and metrics, which macOS models as native_otlp=true, but DefenseClaw does not auto-configure or certify the exporter; Windows remains native_otlp=false. Cleartext HTTP export is disabled, so the loopback gateway is not auto-wired. Global hooks live under ~/.copilot/hooks by default; workspace hooks are optional.

connectors.label: OpenHands
connectors.summary: Global command hooks with optional workspace-local discovery surfaces.
connectors.hilt: OpenHands has no native ask surface; UserPromptSubmit can receive additionalContext, while PreToolUse and Stop confirm downgrades are audit/TUI-only with raw_action preserved.
connectors.notes: macOS/Linux requires OpenHands >=1.12.0 and uses six v6 hook events. Standalone OpenHands SDK 1.39.1 preserves exporter-only, process-environment native OTLP traces, so the macOS/Linux registry reports native_otlp=true; Setup does not persist the launch environment, no native logs/metrics are claimed, and no stable hook/native correlation attribute is documented. Windows preserves a zero version floor with native_otlp=false, but native Windows Setup is unsupported because DefenseClaw has no WSL connector path. Global ~/.openhands/hooks.json is used by default; optional repo-local .openhands/hooks.json takes precedence and files are not merged. MCP follows OPENHANDS_PERSISTENCE_DIR; skills include user installs and the public-skills cache; file agents use .agents/agents with .openhands/agents as a legacy fallback; third-party instruction files are discovery-only; CLI plugins are N/A.

connectors.label: Antigravity
connectors.summary: Five lifecycle hooks, with documented native ask on PreToolUse.
connectors.hilt: Antigravity documents native ask on PreToolUse only. DefenseClaw does not claim that this response overrides permission-bypass flags without persisted official-client evidence; force_ask is retained only as internal raw_action telemetry.
connectors.notes: DefenseClaw's v2 contract accepts >=1.1.8,<1.1.9 on macOS/Linux; the official installer manifest now publishes 1.1.9, which is rejected as unknown pending contract review. Windows preserves >=1.1.8 with no ceiling but remains not certified. The reviewed contract registers all five documented Antigravity lifecycle events (PreInvocation, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PostInvocation, Stop) in ~/.gemini/config/hooks.json. Only synchronous PreToolUse exposes documented hard deny and native ask decisions; invocation events are context-transform surfaces, PostToolUse is observe-only, and DefenseClaw returns allow for Stop rather than claiming stop blocking. Native macOS is preview with no last_validated_version stamp. MCP and AgentSkills folder form are read/write at documented global/workspace paths; macOS/Linux plugins install to the CLI staging root while Windows plugin mutation is discovery-only. Native OTLP, proxy/firewall/sandbox ownership, custom-agent activation, runtime subagent management, and Gemini CLI custody are N/A.

connectors.label: Devin Desktop (Windsurf)
connectors.summary: Cascade hooks across prompts, commands, code access, and MCP tools.
connectors.hilt: Can block supported hook events but has no native human-approval surface; confirm verdicts fall back explicitly.
connectors.notes: Devin Desktop retains Cascade hooks under ~/.codeium/windsurf/hooks.json. DefenseClaw can map configured availability failures to exit 2 on the five documented pre-hooks; other vendor non-zero exits fail open. Post hooks are non-blocking, Cascade response hooks are asynchronous, and Restricted Mode disables hooks. MCP uses the documented mcp_config.json path; Cascade skills, .devin/.windsurf rules, and AGENTS.md instructions are inventoried. Devin Local plugins/subagents are explicitly outside this Cascade connector.

connectors.label: ZeptoClaw
connectors.summary: API base redirect through the DefenseClaw proxy with response scanning.
connectors.hilt: ZeptoClaw has no native ask surface; confirm uses its explicit fallback with raw_action preserved for TUI/audit review. There is no resumable approval.
connectors.notes: api_base redirect into the DefenseClaw proxy plus response-scan.
